flagship.title: A payload pickup for an autonomous quadcopter
flagship.summary: Our capstone quadcopter, M.A.R.V., flies under motion capture and has to collect a 100 g package with a magnet.
flagship.myPart: I designed the pickup mechanism, from a passive ratchet to a servo winch, and produced the stability and control analysis for the design review.
flagship.team: Team of 4. Each of us owns part of the vehicle; these two pieces are mine.

result.text: for the ratchet pickup, against an 80 g mass budget

flagship.figureCaption: The two pickup concepts, v4 and v5.

flagship.title: Three UAVs, designed and built on my own
flagship.summary: An autonomous mapping UAV, a quadcopter frame with its control tuning, and a thermal-imaging drone for crop irrigation that I am assembling now.
flagship.myPart: All of it: component trade studies, frame design and FEA, Pixhawk integration, mission planning, and tuning from flight logs.
flagship.team: Solo. Nobody assigns these; I set the problem and pay for the parts.

result.text: of flight data behind the PID retune that removed a persistent hover oscillation

flagship.figureCaption: Avionics for the current build, on my desk.

flagship.title: Four analyses, each checked a second way
flagship.summary: A structures lab, a transonic airfoil rebuilt from raw CFD data, a CFD drag study and a root solver. Each has a check built in that could have proved me wrong.
flagship.myPart: My own work throughout, except the root solver, which I wrote with one teammate.
flagship.team: Individual, except the root solver (two of us).

result.text: bending stiffness from carbon reinforcement, for 18.6% more weight

flagship.figureCaption: Flexural rigidity of the plain and reinforced beams, from deflection.

flagship.title: A line-following robot with a hand-written turn
flagship.summary: Follow 1.5 m of tape through an S-bend, turn around at a wall and race the next lane home. The library's turn command was banned, so the 180° turn runs on the gyro and the line sensors.
flagship.myPart: I worked on the race program and its tuning with my team.
flagship.team: Course team. The robot is an XRP kit; the program is ours.

result.text: in a race program that ran hands-off in head-to-head races

flagship.figureCaption: The robot on the bench, plugged in for programming.

more.title: Roomly
more.text: A move-out marketplace where the room is the listing. The seller photographs the room once, a vision model drafts a priced listing for each item, and buyers browse the room in 3D.
more.result: Six photos of my own bedroom became 15 priced items in one pass. I also costed in-app payments before building them: about $0.87 kept on a $120 sale, so I argued for in-person handoff.
more.tools: Next.js · React Three Fiber · Claude vision
more.alt: A student apartment rebuilt in 3D inside the Roomly app, with a price tag floating over each piece of furniture

more.title: SARAH
more.text: A dashboard that runs on my laptop and keeps my job search and daily routine on one screen: one Python server, one HTML page, 47 commits. Built with Claude Code as a pair programmer.
more.result: Traced a bug that hid several records at once to rows being keyed by company and role, and re-keyed them by unique ID. Replaced the server's file blocklist with an allowlist, so it serves one page and nothing else.
more.tools: Python · Notion, Gmail and Calendar APIs
more.alt: The SARAH dashboard's Today screen with sample data: the next task, the day's numbers and a task list
